previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and chronic systolic heart failure was admitted due to recurrent hypoglycemia and syncope, occurring just two days after a prior discharge for the same issue. He was found unconscious at home with a blood sugar of 28 despite correct insulin administration. During the hospital stay, his insulin regimen was simplified by switching from NPH insulin to Lantus, starting at 5 units and titrating up to 6 units daily, along with 1 unit of Humalog with each meal to reduce hypoglycemia risk. His lanthanum dose was increased to 1,500 mg with meals due to elevated phosphorus and PTH levels, and his multivitamin was discontinued. He remained stable, completed a hemodialysis session, and was discharged home with close follow-up, new insulin instructions, and additional diabetes education support.
problems: Poor glycemic control in type 1 diabetes

PERSANTINE MIBI  ___

throbbing abdominal pain, resolved prior to admission to

left ventricular dilatation, slightly worse during stress, 
suggesting transient ischemic dilatation. No perfusion defects 
identified. Global hypokinesis with an LVEF of 41%. Given 
findings, pt underwent cardiac catheterization which revealed 
hypertensive heart disease but no angiographically apparent CAD.

gastroparesis and pt. was continued on home regimen of protonix 
& metoclopromide.

and was continued to sevelamer as per outpatient regimen.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  A ___ man with new right-sided subclavian central line,
check placement.

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph of ___.

SINGLE UPRIGHT VIEW OF THE CHEST AT APPROXIMATELY 1:20 P.M.  A right
subclavian catheter extends into the left brachiocephalic vein rather than
entering the superior vena cava.  Repositioning is required.  There is no
pneumothorax.

The heart is moderately enlarged, unchanged from prior examination.  The lungs
are well expanded without focal consolidation or pleural effusion.  The
mediastinum and hila are unremarkable.  The pulmonary vasculature is not
engorged.

Multiple small high attenuation foci are seen overlying the left upper
quadrant in the region of the stomach and are likely secondary to oral
contrast administration.

IMPRESSION:  Right subclavian catheter extending into the left brachiocephalic
vein.  Repositioning is required.  No pneumothorax.  No acute cardiopulmonary
abnormalities.

REASON FOR EXAMINATION:  Follow up of a right central venous line placement.

Portable AP chest radiograph compared to previous study obtained at 1:20.

The right subclavian line still crosses the midline with its tip in the left
brachiocephalic vein.  The rest of the findings are unchanged.  Findings were
communicated to Dr. ___ by Dr. ___.
